Base Class Methods of the Marginal Generics

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
penalty_dhessian.penalty.Rd

The methods of the base class for the four generics that a marginal criterion requires beyond the second order. penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian() and penalty_dcross() each signal an error that names the penalty and the generic; beta_quadratic() returns FALSE. scad_penalty() and mcp_penalty() register none of the four and reach these methods.

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object of a class that registers none of these methods.

beta

A numeric vector of coefficients. Unused.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values. Unused.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian() and penalty_dcross() signal an error. beta_quadratic() returns the single logical FALSE.

Details

A marginal criterion based on a Laplace approximation requires derivatives of the penalty beyond the second order. For a penalty that does not supply them, these methods signal an error, so the hyperparameters of such a penalty cannot be estimated by a marginal criterion. The message of penalty_dhessian() states that consequence; the messages of penalty_d2hessian() and penalty_dcross() name only the penalty and the generic.

The FALSE of beta_quadratic() is the conservative default: a penalty class without a method of its own is treated as having a third \(\beta\)-derivative.

See also

penalty_dhessian() and its siblings for the generics, penalty_dhessian.QuadraticPenalty() for a branch that supplies them.
